newsitem.title: UK: Boots says it is not a proper defendant.
newsitem.headline: Boots says it is not a proper defendant.

text.p: British retailer and pharmacist Boots Co Plc said on Monday that it was not a "proper defendant" in a U.S. lawsuit over the thyroid drug Synthroid.

In a statement Boots said, "The suggestion that Boots has been involved in any anti-trust or racketeering activity in connection with this matter is absurd and the idea that there may be multi-billion dollar liabilities involved is fanciful."
Boots was named in the $8.5 billion suit along with the German chemicals giant BASF AG and its subsidiary Knoll Pharmaceuticals.

The suit, brought by thyroid sufferers, alleges that the three concealed a 1990 University of California study, which concluded that Synthroid was no better at treating hypothyroidism than cheaper generic drugs.
Boots acquired Synthroid in 1986 and sold it to BASF in March 1995, when Knoll acquired all of Boots's pharmaceuticals operations.
"Boots believes there is no merit in the claims made and will vigorously defend them on jurisdictional and, if necessary, substantive grounds."
The company said it had been advised that the report, known as the Dong study, was "scientifically flawed."

"Knoll Pharmaceuticals shares that view and published a rebuttal of the Dong conclusions when the study was published, with Knoll's consent, in the journal of the American Medical Association on April 16," the statement said.
